Construct a multiverse

Source: R/constructor.R
multiverse-constructor.Rd

A multiverse is a collection of related schemas. It is never authored from scratch: as_multiverse() collects schemas you already have, and expand_tines() derives one from a schema and an alternatives file. new_multiverse() is the low-level constructor.

Usage

new_multiverse(schemas = list())

as_multiverse(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_multiverse(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiverse'
as_multiverse(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'schema'
as_multiverse(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'list'
as_multiverse(x, ...)

Arguments

schemas

A list of schema objects.

x

A schema, a multiverse, or a list of either to be coerced.

...

Passed on to methods.

Value

An object of class c("multiverse", "list").

Details

Branches follow list conventions – they may be named or not, exactly as the list you pass in leaves them.

See also

build_schema() to make the schemas in the first place.

Examples

s1 <- example_schema()
s2 <- example_football()

as_multiverse(list(hdi = s1, football = s2))
#> A multiverse with 2 schemas:
#>   hdi: "HDI Example" (3 steps)
#>   football: (3 steps)

# names are optional, as in any list
as_multiverse(list(s1, s2))
#> A multiverse with 2 schemas:
#>   [[1]]: "HDI Example" (3 steps)
#>   [[2]]: (3 steps)
